questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Kazakhstan?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kazakhstan article.

questions.proof: Astana is the capital city of Kazakhstan.

questions.prompt: True or false: “The capital city of Kazakhstan is Astana.”

hints.nudge: Read the statement slowly. Does it match what the article says, or has one word been swapped for another?
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kazakhstan article, or on the Atlas.

questions.proof: The capital city of Kazakhstan is Astana.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Kazakhstan about 2,724,910 square kilometres; Mexico about 1,960,647 square kilometres; Turkey about 783,562 square kilometres; Latvia about 64,594 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Astana?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Kazakhstan is Astana.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Kazakhstan?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Kazakhstan is the Kazakhstani tenge.
